The most likely corrupted element is the tail current source M5. The simulated slew of 1.154e+07 V/s with a 2 pF load implies about 23 µA of tail current, while the M5/M6 width ratio (3.436/1.139 ≈ 3.02) predicts about 30 µA from the 10 µA reference. That shortfall points to the tail path, and the same tail current sets both the slew rate and the gm1 that limits UGBW (24.7 MHz vs. 43 MHz required). The DC gain and phase margin still pass, which fits a reduced-current fault rather than a change to the load or the output stage. I can't tell from these numbers alone whether M5 or its reference M6 was altered, so M6 is ranked second, with the input pair M1 third.
